fields.v: Shepard, A., Albrecht, J. (2026). Probe-and-Refine Tuning of Repository Guidance for Coding Agents. arXiv:2606.20512v2 [cs.SE], 19 Jun 2026 (preprint dated 23 Jun 2026)
Preprint — arXiv:2606.20512v2 [cs.SE] ('A PREPRINT', dated June 23, 2026); no published venue found
Williams College (both authors)

Proposes an approach; secondary: Compares — probe-and-refine tuning of an AGENTS.md-style guidance file, compared with a static knowledge base and no guidance on SWE-bench Verified (4 trials at 200 steps); also step-budget and cross-model (Nemotron) experiments

(1) probe_refined: probe-and-refine tuning (authors' own; code github.com/asashepard/probe-and-refine-tuning), no version. (2) static_kb: authors' two-layer static knowledge base (tree-sitter structural summary + one-shot LLM generic advice), also the starting point of (1). (3) no_context baseline. Guidance described as an AGENTS.md file; no SDD framework

One natural-language repository guidance file per repository (AGENTS.md), capped at 3,000 characters (~750 tokens): structural layer (hubs, entry points, import relationships), procedural rules, and after refinement repo-specific rules (test paths, subsystem tracing) and quality gates. Mean length static_kb 1,687 chars, probe_refined 2,754 chars. Added lines: procedural 47%, structural 30%, quality gate 23% (104 lines)

Tuning (per repository, 3-5 iterations of ~22 single-shot LLM calls, no agent loop or tools): 1 generate 10 synthetic bug-fix probes (temperature 0.9, deduplicated); 2 attempt a fix per probe; 3 judge each attempt and propose edits; 4 aggregate, merge, cap at 5 edits, apply mechanically and trim to 3,000 chars; stop after two iterations without change. Use: guidance given to a fixed ReAct-style coding agent that resolves the issue; single-shot fallback if no patch within the step budget; patches sanitised and evaluated by the SWE-bench harness
None (fully automatic tuning; guidance not reviewed by humans)
Single artefact (context/guidance file), generated and run with an agent
Not classifiable (repository guidance file without a specification; authors use no SDD terms)
Existing code bases: issue resolution (bug fixes and small feature requests) from GitHub issues

SWE-bench Verified, 500 instances, 12 repositories (Django 231 = 46%; seaborn 2, flask 1); guidance from one pinned commit per repository. Unique probe-refined solves: median patch 5 added lines, 13% multi-file
Open-source Python repositories (django, sympy, sphinx, matplotlib, scikit-learn, astropy, xarray, pytest, pylint, requests, seaborn, flask)
N/A (autonomous agent, no participants)

Relative prompt tokens only: probe_refined ~56% more prompt tokens than no_context at 200 steps; tokens at 200 vs 25 steps 2.3x (no_context) and 2.8x (probe_refined). Tuning cost: 3-5 iterations x ~22 calls, ~8k input and ~2k output tokens per call. Steps per instance (Nemotron transfer). No time or money
Resolve rate (% instances whose patch passes SWE-bench held-out tests); coverage (% instances with an evaluable patch); precision (resolved / evaluated); unique consistent solves (>=3 of 4 trials)
Not measured
Not measured

Fallback rate; patch timing (share after step 100); guidance length and content categories; tuning loop output (iterations, probes, edits); agent behaviour under transfer (no-command prose events, stalls, max-step hits, patch-apply errors); localization analysis of unique solves (observed/expected per repository)

Automatic: official SWE-bench Verified harness; agent logs. Manual/qualitative: categorisation of 104 added guidance lines; reading of 31 unique-solve problem statements; analysis of 43 no_context regressions (who coded not stated)

Metric: SWE-bench Verified hidden tests (resolve rate, 500 instances); coverage and precision; cost only as relative prompt tokens. The authors state no success threshold (they stress the relative comparison, absolute rates being low by design, p. 4), so no verdict is given. Agent = authors' ReAct-style bash scaffold (unnamed, released code), 16k effective context, temperature 0. Values: resolve / coverage / precision, mean +- SD of 4 trials at 200 steps unless noted.
Main experiment (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B, 200 steps, 4 trials; Tables 4, 8):
- no_context (baseline) + own scaffold + Qwen3.5-35B-A3B: 25.5 +- 2.2% / 41.7 +- 2.9% / 61.0 +- 2.6%; fallback 25.6%; tokens 2.3x at 200 vs 25 steps. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- static_kb + own scaffold + Qwen3.5-35B-A3B: 28.3 +- 1.4% / 50.6 +- 2.3% / 56.0 +- 2.5%; fallback 30.8%. Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors (one-off generation per repository, not quantified)
- probe_refined + own scaffold + Qwen3.5-35B-A3B: 33.0 +- 1.8% / 56.2 +- 1.8% / 58.6 +- 1.6%; fallback 14.8%; ~56% more prompt tokens than no_context; tokens 2.8x at 200 vs 25 steps; tuning 3-5 iterations x ~22 calls of ~8k/2k tokens per repository (one-off). Quality: no criterion stated by the authors; cost: no criterion stated by the authors
Step-budget runs (Qwen, single trial; Table 9), resolve at 25 / 50 / 100 steps:
- no_context: 24.4 / 27.6 / 23.6%
- static_kb: 21.8 / 29.8 / 29.6%
- probe_refined: 24.2 / 23.4 / 30.8% (below static_kb at 50 steps, p=0.022)
- Quality and cost for all: no criterion stated by the authors
Cross-model (NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B, 200 steps, single trial; Tables 11-12):
- no_context + own scaffold + Nemotron: 28.4% (142 resolved). Quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- static_kb + own scaffold + Nemotron: 24.6%. Quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- probe_refined (Nemotron-tuned) + own scaffold + Nemotron: 27.0% (135); tuning loop degraded (3.8 of 5 iterations); 351 agent-loop patches, 3 fallback, 39.2 steps per instance, 11 hit max steps; agent-loop precision 38.5%. Quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors
- probe_refined (Qwen-tuned, transferred) + own scaffold + Nemotron: 13.2% (66); 174 agent-loop patches, 324 fallback patches (none resolved); 81.0 steps per instance, 83 hit max steps; agent-loop precision 37.9%. Quality and cost: no criterion stated by the authors (the authors call it a 'collapse', p. 16)
fields.why: The partly/does-not-work verdicts were the extractor's own cut-offs (r2 'why' says so); the paper states no success criterion, so per the 2026-11-23 rule every verdict is 'no criterion stated by the authors'. Values kept. Also fixed: r2 attached 39.2 steps per instance to Nemotron no_context, but in Table 12 the 'Nemotron baseline' column is the Nemotron self-tuned probe_refined run (135 resolved = 27.0%)

fields.v: Tasks: SWE-bench Verified 500 instances. Configurations: 3 guidance conditions x Qwen3.5-35B-A3B (4 trials at 200 steps; single trials at 25/50/100 steps) and x Nemotron (single trial, plus Qwen-to-Nemotron transfer). Baseline: no_context. Held constant: scaffold, model within experiment, harness, 16k context, 2,048 output tokens per turn, output truncation ~3,000 chars, temperature 0 (0.9 for probes), same hardware; guidance tuned with the consuming model. Acceptance: SWE-bench held-out tests. Repetitions: 4 (main), 1 (others). Human intervention: none. Statistics: mixed-effects logistic regression (instance and trial random effects, n=6,000), per-trial McNemar, Wilson CIs

Qwen, 200 steps: probe_refined 33.0% > static_kb 28.3% > no_context 25.5% in 4/4 trials; mixed-effects OR 2.11 (vs no_context, p<0.001), 1.58 (vs static_kb, p<0.001), static_kb vs no_context OR 1.34 (p=0.004). Gain of 7.5 pp = 2.8 static_kb + 4.7 refinement. Coverage +14.5 pp; precision not significantly different (p=0.119). Unique consistent solves 31 vs 8 (no_context) vs 4 (static_kb); easy core 65, hard core 342. Effect present for Django (27.7/31.2/35.3%) and non-Django (23.5/25.8/30.9%). Budget: all equal at 25 steps; no_context flat; probe_refined only one rising beyond 100 steps. Nemotron: ordering reversed (28.4 > 27.0 > 24.6%); Qwen-tuned guidance collapses Nemotron to 13.2%

Distinguished conditions at 200 steps with 4 trials (consistent ordering, significant); budget and cross-model results single-trial, descriptive. Limitations stated: guidance length confound (refined 63% longer; padding/truncation ablations not run); localization hypothesis not causally tested (file-structure ablation not run); one model able to run the procedure; loop prompts tuned to Qwen; no probe/seed sensitivity analysis; single benchmark with Django concentration; contamination cannot be ruled out; constrained pipeline (16k context) gives low absolute rates

Variance only characterised by 4 trials; lower budgets single trial; length confound open; procedure shown on one model; Nemotron-adapted prompts untested; other scaffolds (summarisation, tree search) may differ; probe sensitivity untested; SWE-bench Verified only, Django 46%; 42% of instances unreachable by guidance. Future: file-structure ablation (highest priority), larger dense model, multi-model tuning, balanced benchmarks

Tables 4, 6, 9-12 jumbled by pdftotext; values rebuilt from column order and text. Fig. 7 labels 32.9% where text and tables give 33.0%. Nemotron single trial justified by 'trial-level variance is negligible at n=500', while Qwen SDs are 1.4-2.9 pp and T2 differs from other trials. Introduction reports Gloaguen et al.'s drop as ~3%. Code released (GitHub); no data package or pre-registration stated. Programming language: Python

Partly (0.5): main results support the claims and negative results reported; but generalisations ('instructions matter at least as much as reasoning', guidance encodes model-specific calibration) rest on one capable model and single-trial cross-model runs
fields.why: Main claims follow from the 4-trial results and negative findings are reported (50-step dip, Nemotron reversal, transfer collapse), which supports Yes; but the conclusion that instructions 'matter at least as much as the agents' own reasoning' (p. 19) and that guidance encodes model-specific calibration (p. 17) rest on one tuning-capable model and single-trial cross-model runs. Partly kept
fields.doubt: Os resultados principais (4 ensaios) suportam as conclusões e os negativos são relatados; mas generalizações (p. 17 e 19) assentam num só modelo e em ensaios únicos com Nemotron. Decide entre Partly e Yes.

fields.why: Both guided conditions (probe_refined, static_kb) and the agent scaffold are the authors' own; the only baseline (no_context) is the authors' scaffold without guidance, not an external tool. No follows if this baseline is not an external approach; the 2026-11-23 rule gives Partly when the own approach is compared with external baselines, and a reader could count no_context (or the third-party models Qwen/Nemotron) as such
fields.doubt: Todas as condições usam o scaffold dos próprios autores; o baseline no_context é esse scaffold sem orientação. Decide se conta como baseline externo (Partly) ou não (No).
